items.lesson: Frozen semantic Hook positively activated and deferred on two valid explicit contract-negative prefixes (a joint and a single-entity question), misclassifying explicit negatives as evidence gaps, while intended positive cases never activated. Narrow boundary: the Hook cannot selectively gate one-sided two-candidate gaps without over-triggering on explicit negatives. Hypothesis Researcher: do not rely unchanged; add a deterministic explicit-negative guard or run a specified recheck.
items.applicability: Scope: frozen semantic Hook in two-candidate evaluation on valid explicit contract-negative joint and single-entity questions, faithful wiring. Recheck: a Hook variant that passes explicit-negative prefixes without activation (verified on matched positives) or a deterministic negative pre-filter.

items.lesson: Semantic-Hook detection of genuine one-sided two-candidate evidence gaps lacks selectivity and utility: activations occurred only on explicit negatives (one directly regressed), no intended positive behavior appeared, and gains came only from Hook-negative no-op runs while accuracy declined and Hook cost rose sharply. Disposition: stop unchanged; revisit only with activation-attributed benefit on positives and no negative over-trigger.
items.applicability: Mechanism class: semantic Hook gating of one-sided evidence gaps in two-candidate review; contract-negative joint/single-entity cases plus aggregate accuracy/cost. Revisit: activation-attributed benefit over matched controls with no negative over-trigger.

required_concepts: semantic classifier fires on explicit negatives

items.lesson: The frozen semantic Hook model repeatedly misclassifies explicit contract negatives as deferral-worthy: two valid explicit-negative questions (one joint, one single-entity) both produced Hook-positive activations, one directly regressing the trajectory, with no positive-case activation observed. The Hook cannot separate explicit negatives from genuine one-sided gaps. Hypothesis Researcher: do not rely unchanged; add a deterministic guard on explicit contract-negative inputs before reuse.
items.applicability: Observed for the Hook model's three-way deferral decisions in valid evaluation prefixes with explicit contract-negative joint and single-entity questions; limit releases only with a wider matched probe including true one-sided-gap positives or a deterministic guard.

items.lesson: Semantic-Hook deferral for one-sided two-candidate evidence gaps carries no attributed utility: accuracy declined, Hook cost rose sharply, and every improvement came from Hook-negative no-op runs while activations hit only explicit negatives. Stop unchanged; revisit only with activation-attributed positive-case benefit, bounded Hook cost, and demonstrated selectivity on explicit negatives.
items.applicability: Applies to semantic-Hook deferral mechanisms in candidate evaluation over contract-negative joint and single-entity questions; does not extend to Hook variants that never fire or settings without per-activation cost and utility attribution.
